lines.text: On the Kola Peninsula, above the Arctic Circle, there's a hole you could cover with a dinner plate.
lines.cue: caption: COVER IT WITH A PLATE

lines.text: It's about twenty-three centimetres across, and twelve thousand two hundred and sixty-two metres deep.
Drop the deepest point of the ocean in, and you'd still have more than a kilometre to spare.
And it isn't even a third of the way through the crust.
lines.cue: caption: NOT EVEN 1/3 OF THE CRUST

lines.text: Engineers spent about twenty years digging it. Then they stopped.
Not because they ran out of planet. Something down there fought back.
So what stopped the deepest hole ever dug? The full video has the answer.
